title: Building a Sustainable Psychological Life: Habit, Meaning, Seeking Help
summary: Mental health is not just the absence of illness; it is built through things you can help your teen with: (1) Daily habits: 7-9 hours of sleep, 30 minutes of movement, healthy food, and real connection with people. (2) Meaning: help them discover what gives them purpose (service, knowledge, art, family) — meaning protects against emptiness. (3) A professional network: a therapist or counsellor they trust, a psychiatrist whose number they know, and your country's mental-health helpline saved on their phone. (4) Seeking help is strength: teach them that saying "I need help" is maturity, not weakness. Your teen is building a life, not just passing through a phase.
try_this: This week: Encourage your teen to write a "self-contract": 3 daily habits, one value to live by, a person they trust, and your country's emergency number. They sign it and review it every month.
reflection_prompts: Which three habits has your teen committed to?
What value has your teen chosen to live by in the coming year?
